units.rhetorical_move: opens with a slogan and a definition
units.function: sets the tone before the problem

original_instantiations: A short slogan states that the services count, and a definition follows.
The opening line is a claim, not a summary of the method.

units.source_excerpt: Ecosystem services matters! Sustainability is necessary
units.reusable_pattern: Open with a short claim, then define the term.
prohibited_generalizations: do not open a technical paper with an unargued slogan

units.rhetorical_move: says the small effects add up
units.function: turns a negligible single case into a cumulative harm

original_instantiations: Each project looks small against the whole biosphere, yet together they cut the diversity.
The concession comes first and the reversal second.

units.source_excerpt: The impact of these projects of varying sizes may seem negligible to the total ability of the biosphere's functioning potential, cumulatively they are directly impacting the biodiversity
units.reusable_pattern: Grant the smallness, then reverse it with the cumulative effect.
prohibited_generalizations: do not drop the concession

units.rhetorical_move: announces the method chain
units.function: names each technique and what it produces

original_instantiations: One classification builds the index, two weighting methods combine it, and a clustering grades it.
Each technique is named with its output.

units.source_excerpt: To begin with, in order to measure the impact numerically, we introduce a classification method to make up the index. Furthermore, the indicators are integrated by two weighting methods.
units.reusable_pattern: Start the chain with to begin with and add each step with furthermore.
prohibited_generalizations: do not name a method without its output

units.rhetorical_move: reports the grades of the four projects
units.function: lets the result arrive as a finding

original_instantiations: Two projects grade weak, one moderate and one strong.
The finding is stated after the method, not before.

units.source_excerpt: As a result, we found that the relocation project and the house construction belong to weak, the factory construction is moderate and the pipeline engineering is strong.
units.reusable_pattern: Introduce the finding with as a result.
prohibited_generalizations: do not state the grades before the method

units.rhetorical_move: reads the forecast as a life cycle
units.function: gives the year of the peak and the year of the end

original_instantiations: Without the services the ratio peaks in one year and dies in another, and with them it keeps rising.
The two cases are set against each other by their years.

units.source_excerpt: The result shows that considering the cost has the accumulation of a long life cycle and high efficiency. Without considering it, the ratio reaches its maximum in one year and stops making profits later.
units.reusable_pattern: Report the result, then the two cases with their years.
prohibited_generalizations: do not give the years without the cases

units.rhetorical_move: claims the factor grows with the size
units.function: treats the four values as obvious evidence

original_instantiations: The four values rise with the size of the project, and the rise is called obvious.
The claim rests on the order of the numbers.

units.source_excerpt: Eventually, the values of the factor for the four projects are given, and it is obvious that the factor increases as the size of the project increases.
units.reusable_pattern: List the values, then call the pattern obvious.
prohibited_generalizations: do not call a pattern obvious when one value breaks it

units.rhetorical_move: lists what the ecosystem does
units.function: builds the stakes from three services

original_instantiations: The system gives space, supplies resources and takes in the waste.
The three services are listed before the problem.

units.source_excerpt: It not only provides space for human survival, but also provides various resources needed for human development, and absorbs waste generated by human production and life.
units.reusable_pattern: List the services with not only and but also.
prohibited_generalizations: do not stop at one service

units.rhetorical_move: turns the gap into a question worth asking
units.function: closes the background with the question

original_instantiations: Most projects ignore the services, so the question of the real value is worth asking.
The question is the last line of the background.

units.source_excerpt: Therefore, how to evaluate the environmental cost of land use development projects and determine the real valuation of projects is worth our consideration
units.reusable_pattern: Close with therefore and a how-to question.
prohibited_generalizations: do not answer the question in the same sentence

units.rhetorical_move: restates the task with a purpose clause
units.function: says what the model must determine

original_instantiations: The model is built so the real cost can be understood, and it has to grade a project.
The purpose comes before the requirement.

units.source_excerpt: For the sake of understanding the real economic costs of land use projects in ecosystem services, we are required to establish an ecological services valuation model which determines a project's quality.
units.reusable_pattern: Lead with for the sake of and follow with the requirement.
prohibited_generalizations: do not add tasks the problem did not set

units.rhetorical_move: lays out the work in three stages
units.function: gives the reader the order of the paper

original_instantiations: The first stage builds the system, the second the valuation, the third the factor.
Each stage is one block.

units.source_excerpt: We will proceed as follows to tackle these problems
units.reusable_pattern: Announce the plan, then number the stages.
prohibited_generalizations: do not let a stage carry two jobs

units.rhetorical_move: justifies the assumptions before listing them
units.function: claims each one is defended

original_instantiations: The assumptions are made to simplify the problem and to mimic real conditions, and each one is said to be defended.
The defence is promised before the list.

units.source_excerpt: To simplify the problem and make it convenient for us to simulate real-life conditions, we make the following basic assumptions, each of which is properly justified.
units.reusable_pattern: Give the purpose and promise the justification.
reusable_elements: each of which is properly justified
prohibited_generalizations: do not promise a justification the bullet does not give

units.rhetorical_move: trusts the data because the sources are trusted
units.function: converts source trust into metric trust

original_instantiations: The data are trusted because the sources are trusted, so the metrics are trusted too.
The confidence is inherited, not tested.

units.source_excerpt: We assume all data we obtain are trustworthy since all of sources are reliable. Thus, we are confident that our metrics can reflect the accurate condition.
units.reusable_pattern: Ground the trust in the sources, then extend it.
prohibited_generalizations: do not treat source trust as a test of the model

units.rhetorical_move: points the reader to the table
units.function: keeps the prose out of the definitions

original_instantiations: The symbols are collected in one table and the prose only points to it.
No definition is repeated in the sentence.

units.source_excerpt: We list the symbols and notations used in this paper in Table 1.
units.reusable_pattern: Point to the table and stop.
prohibited_generalizations: do not redefine the symbols in prose

units.rhetorical_move: states the aim and the pipeline
units.function: names the index before the methods

original_instantiations: The index is built so the impact can be measured, and the clustering grades it.
The aim comes first and the pipeline second.

units.source_excerpt: In this section, in order to measure the impact of ecosystem services, we make up the ecosystem services index.
units.reusable_pattern: Open the section with the aim.
prohibited_generalizations: do not start with the algebra

units.rhetorical_move: credits the borrowed classification
units.function: says why that classification was chosen

original_instantiations: The borrowed classification is chosen because it ties the services to human well-being.
The reason follows the credit.

units.source_excerpt: According to the classification method of the published assessment, the classification framework combines ecosystem services with human well-being, and the classification system is more systematic.
units.reusable_pattern: Credit the source and give the reason for the choice.
prohibited_generalizations: do not drop the citation

units.rhetorical_move: justifies one indicator by its status
units.function: turns importance into a reason for inclusion

original_instantiations: Food dominates agricultural production, so its ratio is brought in.
The status of the thing is the reason for the indicator.

units.source_excerpt: Food is the main component of the ecosystem, and its status in agricultural production determines that its development and utilization is a significant engineering design. Therefore, we introduce the ratio of food production.
units.reusable_pattern: State the status, then the indicator it justifies.
prohibited_generalizations: do not add an indicator without a reason

units.rhetorical_move: explains why the normalization is done
units.function: promises that the number alone will show the merit

original_instantiations: After the normalization, the merit of an indicator can be read straight from its number.
The convenience is the stated payoff.

units.source_excerpt: Therefore, it is convenient to judge the merits of the evaluation indicators directly from the numerical value, and facilitate the evaluation of multi-attribute decision-making.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the payoff of the preprocessing.
prohibited_generalizations: do not claim the number removes every judgement

units.rhetorical_move: says why the deviation cannot be used
units.function: replaces it with a ratio

original_instantiations: The deviation cannot compare groups with different units, but its ratio to the mean can.
The rejection and the replacement share one sentence.

units.source_excerpt: Considering the difference between the units and the mean, the standard deviation cannot be used to compare the degree of variation, but the ratio of the standard deviation to the mean is used to compare.
units.reusable_pattern: Reject one measure and offer the ratio.
prohibited_generalizations: do not use the rejected measure later

units.rhetorical_move: reads the weight table
units.function: ranks the groups from the numbers

original_instantiations: The weights sit near one value, one indicator leads, and the four groups fall in an order.
The reading names the leader and the order.

units.source_excerpt: As can be seen from the table below, the weight difference between the indicators is not big. One service ranks first, another follows, and the rest come after.
units.reusable_pattern: Point at the table and read the order.
prohibited_generalizations: do not invent an order the table does not show

units.rhetorical_move: explains the clustering by an image
units.function: makes the algorithm sound like a tree

original_instantiations: The clustering grows a tree from single leaves up to the roots.
The image comes before the complexity.

units.source_excerpt: Hierarchical clustering algorithm is just like building a branching tree from bottom up, with leaves as individual documents and the centers as the roots.
units.reusable_pattern: Explain the algorithm by one image.
prohibited_generalizations: do not leave the image unexplained

units.rhetorical_move: gives the grade boundaries
units.function: turns the index into three grades

original_instantiations: Below the first threshold the project is weak, between the two it is moderate, and above the second it is strong.
Each grade gets its own sentence.

units.source_excerpt: When the score is less than the first threshold, it is a weak project. While the score is between the two thresholds, it is a moderate project. In the condition that the score is more than the second, it is regarded as strong.
units.reusable_pattern: State each grade with its range.
prohibited_generalizations: do not leave a gap between the ranges

units.rhetorical_move: matches the grade to reality
units.function: uses the match as support

original_instantiations: The largest project grades strong, and that agrees with what is already known.
The agreement is offered as evidence.

units.source_excerpt: The project construction is very complex, with a long construction period and high technical requirements, therefore it has the greatest impact on the environment and the intensity is strong which is in line with reality.
units.reusable_pattern: Give the reason, the grade, then the agreement.
prohibited_generalizations: do not treat agreement with expectation as a test

units.rhetorical_move: matches the small project the same way
units.function: repeats the support for the other end

original_instantiations: The smallest project grades weak, and that too agrees with what is known.
The same move is used at both ends.

units.source_excerpt: Its impact on the environment is relatively small, so the intensity of ecosystem services is weak which corresponds to reality.
units.reusable_pattern: Give the reason and the agreement.
prohibited_generalizations: do not use a different standard for the small project

units.rhetorical_move: splits the cost into internal and external
units.function: says the external cost is a loss of productivity

original_instantiations: The internal cost is what the developer pays and the external cost is the loss caused elsewhere.
The contrast fixes where each cost shows up.

units.source_excerpt: The external cost is not directly reflected in the expenditure of land development itself, but in the monetary estimate of other environmental losses caused by the development of land.
units.reusable_pattern: Define the external cost by where it does not appear.
prohibited_generalizations: do not price the external cost as a direct expense

units.rhetorical_move: reads the fitted curve in three stages
units.function: narrates the slow, the fast and the slow again

original_instantiations: The index rises slowly, then fast, then slowly again as the cost grows.
Each stage gets a reason.

units.source_excerpt: From the above figure, we can see that the services and the original costs match the tendency of a growth curve approximately. At first the index increases slowly, then rapidly, and then tends to be slow.
units.reusable_pattern: Point at the figure and narrate the stages.
prohibited_generalizations: do not narrate a rise the fitted curve does not show

units.rhetorical_move: contrasts the two life cycles
units.function: says the counted case lasts longer

original_instantiations: Without the services the benefit rises and then falls, but with them it keeps rising for a long time.
The contrast is the whole point.

units.source_excerpt: Without considering the cost, the benefit tends to increase first and then decrease. However, if the enterprise takes the services into consideration, the benefits will gradually increase over time, and the trend of growth will continue for a long time.
units.reusable_pattern: Set the two cases against each other with however.
prohibited_generalizations: do not merge the two curves

units.rhetorical_move: praises the method against the rivals
units.function: lists the faults the method avoids

original_instantiations: The method rests on a stronger principle and avoids the overfitting and the slow convergence of the rivals.
The rivals are named by their faults.

units.source_excerpt: Unlike traditional machine learning methods that follow the principle of empirical risk minimization, the method avoids problems such as overfitting, difficult parameter adjustment and slow convergence.
units.reusable_pattern: Contrast the method with the rivals and list the avoided faults.
prohibited_generalizations: do not claim the faults were tested

units.rhetorical_move: reads the forecast as a delayed decline
units.function: says the services lengthen the life

original_instantiations: The forecast keeps rising for nearly two decades, so the decline is delayed.
The reading names the effect on the life cycle.

units.source_excerpt: It can be seen that considering the services can effectively increase the life cycle of the project, consolidate the existing status, and delay the arrival of the recession.
units.reusable_pattern: Draw the conclusion with it can be seen that.
prohibited_generalizations: do not claim the forecast was tested against later data

units.rhetorical_move: reads the crossing of the two curves
units.function: marks the year where the two cases meet

original_instantiations: The curves meet in one year, and after that the counted case stays above.
The crossing is given a meaning.

units.source_excerpt: In one year the two curves intersect, indicating the benefit-cost of the two cases is equivalent at this time. After that, the benefits brought by the service should be greater.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the crossing and what it indicates.
prohibited_generalizations: do not move the crossing year

units.rhetorical_move: reads the end of the uncounted case
units.function: gives the year the ratio hits zero

original_instantiations: By a stated year the uncounted case has damaged the environment enough that the ratio hits zero.
The zero is tied to the damage.

units.source_excerpt: When reaching that year, not considering the services will lead to the destruction of the environment seriously affecting the operation, so that the ratio reaches zero.
units.reusable_pattern: Give the year, the cause and the zero.
prohibited_generalizations: do not give the zero without the cause

units.rhetorical_move: reads the share from the chart
units.function: gives one project's split as the example

original_instantiations: The share of sustainable measures rises with the scale, and one project is almost entirely sustainable.
The example carries the numbers.

units.source_excerpt: As the scale of the project increases, the proportion of projects adopting sustainable measures is also increasing. For example, one project takes such measures for most of the total, and the rest for only a small share.
units.reusable_pattern: State the trend, then the example.
prohibited_generalizations: do not state the trend without a number

units.rhetorical_move: reads the exponential growth
units.function: says the gap between sizes widens

original_instantiations: The large project's benefit grows exponentially and the gap with the smaller ones widens.
The reading is about the gap, not the level.

units.source_excerpt: As can be seen from the figure, for the large project the benefits of adopting sustainable measures will grow exponentially over time, and the gap between medium and small scale will increase.
units.reusable_pattern: Point at the figure and name the gap.
prohibited_generalizations: do not claim the small project grows fastest

units.rhetorical_move: says the factor has an optimal value
units.function: reads the shrinking gap as saturation

original_instantiations: The curves draw closer as the factor grows, so a larger factor is not always better.
The shrinking gap is the evidence.

units.source_excerpt: With the increase of the factor, the ratio of the same project grows increasingly slowly, that is, the area between two adjacent curves gradually shrinks. This means that the value of the factor is not the larger the better, but there is an optimal value.
units.reusable_pattern: Describe the shrinking, then the reading.
prohibited_generalizations: do not name an optimal value the figure does not mark

units.rhetorical_move: appeals to a natural law
units.function: treats the agreement as proof of stability

original_instantiations: The narrowing agrees with how natural things develop, and that is taken to show the model is stable.
The appeal replaces a test.

units.source_excerpt: The distance between adjacent curves is gradually narrowing which also accord with the development law of natural thing. This shows the stability of our model, which can solve practical problems in real life.
units.reusable_pattern: Appeal to the general law, then claim the stability.
prohibited_generalizations: do not treat a general law as a validation

units.rhetorical_move: balances the higher cost against the longer life
units.function: turns the balance into a suggestion

original_instantiations: Counting the services raises the cost, but over time it lengthens the life and the cumulative benefit.
The concession comes before the suggestion.

units.source_excerpt: Although considering the services increases the cost of land use projects, in the long run it will increase the project life cycle and cumulative benefits. Therefore, we suggest that the emphasis on sustainable development factors will contribute to the long-term development.
units.reusable_pattern: Concede the cost, then give the suggestion.
prohibited_generalizations: do not hide the higher cost

units.rhetorical_move: gives the managers three stages
units.function: orders the advice by the life of the project

original_instantiations: First take the current workload as the benchmark, then staff by familiarity, then adjust the posts once the work is stable.
The three stages follow the project.

units.source_excerpt: First of all, we should take the workload of the existing projects as the benchmark. Secondly, it should be configured according to the familiarity of personnel with the posts. Finally, post adjustment can be made.
units.reusable_pattern: Number the advice by the stage of the project.
prohibited_generalizations: do not give the advice out of order

units.rhetorical_move: claims the test shows the model is correct
units.function: lets four projects stand for a proof

original_instantiations: A test on four projects is said to show the model is robust and correct.
The claim is larger than the test.

units.source_excerpt: Test of 4 projects of varying sizes shows that our model is robust and correct.
units.reusable_pattern: Report the test and the claim together.
prohibited_generalizations: do not call four cases a proof

units.rhetorical_move: contrasts the short gain with the long instability
units.function: restates the forecast in words

original_instantiations: The projects that ignore the services earn more at first but grow unsteadily later.
The concession and the reversal share the sentence.

units.source_excerpt: It can be illustrated from the results that after considering the cost, the projects will continue to develop in a stable trend, although the projects without considering the cost have more benefits in the short term, it will develop unsteadily in the long term.
units.reusable_pattern: Lead with the result and concede the short term gain.
prohibited_generalizations: do not drop the although

units.rhetorical_move: claims two methods beat one
units.function: names the harm that is avoided

original_instantiations: Two weighting methods are used so the faults of either one alone are avoided.
The strength is the avoidance.

units.source_excerpt: We use two weighting methods to determine the weight of the indicators, avoiding the negative effects of a single method.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the methods and the harm they avoid.
prohibited_generalizations: do not claim the single method was tested

units.rhetorical_move: claims the cases prove effectiveness
units.function: treats real projects as the validation

original_instantiations: The model is checked on real projects and found highly effective.
The finding is stated as a fact.

units.source_excerpt: We validate our model through real land use project cases and find that our model is highly effective.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the validation and the finding.
prohibited_generalizations: do not upgrade a qualitative match into effectiveness

units.rhetorical_move: blames the data for the missing coverage
units.function: owns the loss of accuracy

original_instantiations: The search data are limited, so the indicators cannot cover the real services and the accuracy may fall.
The cause and the effect are both owned.

units.source_excerpt: Due to the limited search data, the indicators used cannot completely describe the actual ecosystem services, which may reduce the accuracy of our model.
units.reusable_pattern: Give the cause, then the possible loss.
prohibited_generalizations: do not claim the indicators are complete

units.rhetorical_move: admits the missing costs
units.function: names the bias they cause

original_instantiations: Policy costs and disaster costs are left out, so the analysis is biased.
The omission and the bias are paired.

units.source_excerpt: Our model does not take into account the possible costs of policies, natural disasters, etc., so there is a bias in the analysis.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the omitted costs and the bias.
prohibited_generalizations: do not imply the bias was measured

units.rhetorical_move: lists the sources as numbered lines
units.function: keeps articles and books in one list

original_instantiations: Each source gets a number and its own line.
The list mixes articles and books.

units.source_excerpt: [1] de GROOT R S, ALKEMADE R, BRAAT L, et al. Challenges in integrating the concept of ecosystem services and values.
units.reusable_pattern: Give each source a number and one line.
prohibited_generalizations: do not retype the whole list
